message.content:
**Claude Fable 5.1 — Round 3**

**Corrections first.** The secretary's two fact checks against me are right. (i) The fit ends 2024Q1, so the sample holds six zero-labelled inversion-period origins (2022Q4–2024Q1, curve ≈ min12) and none of the re-steepening. My "resolved zeros through 2025Q3" was wrong and my ≤2022Q3 disclosure fit was built on it. (ii) "Stationary bootstrap, mean block 8 = walk-forward convention" was not an existing convention; the repo's only convention is the episode-block bootstrap, seed 42. Both withdrawn. The framing of my positions is otherwise accurate.

**D1 — shadow at all.** Yes. A state that anyone can recompute from FRED forever records nothing about what was believed when; only a fitted forecast tied to a vintage does. Compromise: Claude's hash commitment answers Grok's "monitoring number beside a live P" — nothing with a percent sign is published. I would vote against a text with no shadow, but I will not call that a veto if Grok can live with a hashed, unpublished one.

**D2 — storage.** Move from (a) to (c). My objection to (b) — a diary — is met by a public sha256 per row. Conditions I need in the spec: canonical serialisation of the hashed line (row id, fit-vintage id, `curve_min12`, `p_hukommelse`, snapshot hash) so a reveal is verifiable byte-for-byte; the hash written in the same commit as the ledger row; one line, one hash, no alternates. `curve_min12` itself may stay public — it carries no belief. **Veto:** a private file with no public commitment.

**D3 — scored rule now.** I concede (a), on the matrix's fact: the four block lengths were four new choices and I supplied one of them. What I need written now, as constraints not a bar: sealed before the first onset it counts; ≥ 2 post-sealing onsets; quarterly origins; comparator = operational P from the identical vintage (the matrix shows no separate control is needed); Kimi's fixed stopping rule; the shadow file stays hashed until that council convenes; the repo's episode-block bootstrap, seed 42, named as the default procedure so block length is never shopped. Evidence that would move me back to pinning a number: a showing that a 2028 council cannot credibly seal before onsets in the 2030s — I don't see one.

**D4 — H justification.** Sol is right that backward memory and forward label are distinct quantities; equality at 12 is a coincidence, not identification. Spec text: operative reason is pre-existence (v4); the label-horizon equality recorded as a mnemonic only; E2's three values beside it; "chosen knowing them." I can live with pre-existence alone.

**D5 — ≤2022Q3 fit.** Withdrawn; premise was false. Replacement disclosure, one sentence: the fit sample contains six zero-labelled origins inside the 2022–24 inversion and no origin after it; the 2024Q2+ re-steepening is unresolved and absent.

**D6 — live value.** (b): live trailing month as month 12 plus the 11 previous published months, mirroring exactly how P's live input relates to its fit input. Sol's "new feature" charge applies equally to P's own live curve. I accept (a) if the council prefers; it must be pinned either way and the logged value marked.

**D7 — start.** November 2026, unchanged. With the number hashed, Grok's distribution objection is gone; what remains is Argon's point — a row written before an outcome is known is the only thing that makes any later evaluation prospective. Waiting to September 2027 risks the first row postdating a dated onset.

**Would change my mind on D1/D7:** a demonstrated way to game the hash commitment that the same-commit, one-line-per-row rule does not close.
message.reasoning:
I need to draft Round 3 as Claude Fable 5.1, moving toward convergence, around 600 words. First I should own my own errors—the fit sample actually ends in 2024Q1, not 2025Q3, and the stationary bootstrap claim about mean block size 8 wasn't an established convention—then work through each open dispute D1 through D7 with a final position, possible compromise, and any veto points.

Correcting the sample window matters: the fit actually covers the inversion-period zeros from 2022Q4 through 2024Q1, not the re-steepening period, which undercuts my earlier premise for the ≤2022Q3 disclosure fit since it assumed the re-steepening zeros were included. That changes D5 significantly—since the re-steepening rows aren't yet resolved or eligible, the fit mostly reflects how deeply inverted, no-onset-within-4-quarters origins already attenuate both coefficients, and Sol's objection that this is just another cherry-picked cutoff is fair. I'll concede D5 and drop it, replacing it with a simple disclosure sentence noting the fit contains the handful of inversion-period zero-labeled origins and none from the re-steepening period.

On the bootstrap convention, I realize the repo actually uses an episode-block bootstrap over cycle blocks with a fixed seed rather than the walk-forward mean-8 assumption I'd been using, so I should align with that repo convention wherever a parameter is pinned.

For D1, I'm weighing Grok's objection to including the shadow metric. Since consensus needs all seven to approve, I'm deciding my position: I'd vote to keep the shadow given its near-zero logging cost and the fact that omitting it makes the state harder to reconstruct, but I could accept Claude's hash-commitment compromise as a way to secure Grok's approval, since a hashed value still preserves accountability without fully exposing the live number.

For D2, my earlier round-2 stance favored a public field, but Claude's hash commitment satisfies my diary objection since it's auditable without being published. I'm adding a requirement that the hashed line include the fit vintage id, curve_min12 value, p_hukommelse, and row id under a canonical serialization so the hash can be verified, while keeping curve_min12 itself public since it carries no belief content. Moving to D3, I'm noting my position was to pin the rule now, and the secretary's fact-check flags that block variants count as new choices under the repo's episode-block bootstrap.

Most models (Opus, Sol, Grok, DeepSeek) say no numeric bar is needed, while others (Fable, Kimi, Argon) want a pinned descriptive screen. I'm leaning toward accepting the screen but attaching conditions — sealed timing before onsets, at least two origins, quarterly spacing, identical-vintage comparator, Kimi's stopping rule, and a default bootstrap seed — though I'm wrestling with whether §5.2's requirement for a numerically pinned bar conflicts with calling this just a "descriptive" screen, since 1.96 is itself a number.

Resolving the sealing question: a council can seal the bar before the onsets it judges, since a 2028 council could seal before 2030/2034 onsets and the shadow file stays hidden until then, which satisfies §8.3. I'll concede D3 to option (a) with the condition that the bar seals before the first counted onset and the repo's episode-block bootstrap with seed 42 is fixed as the default so no future council can cherry-pick block lengths.

For D4, I'm backing off treating label-horizon equality as structural justification — it's just a mnemonic coincidence. The spec should record pre-existence as the operative reason, note the label-horizon match separately as a memorable coincidence, and still acknowledge the three E2 values were known in advance.

D5 gets withdrawn since its premise is wrong, replaced with a disclosure sentence about the six inversion zeros. For D6, I'm weighing whether the live value should use only the last 12 published monthly GS10−TB3MS figures excluding the live trailing month, versus including it.

The real tension is that the operational pipeline uses the live trailing month of daily DGS10−DTB3, while calibration fits on monthly aggregates — so there's a mismatch between how the live input relates to the fit input. Including the live month as month 12 matches what I argued in Round 2 for monthly operational aggregation, but Sol considers that a new feature, and whether the hash-committed H=12 window lags by a month comes down to whether today's live month gets counted — though since both current values are positive, it doesn't change anything materially right now.

For D7, I'd lean toward holding November with the hash commitment, since that neutralizes Grok's objection and preserves Argon's point that the prospective nature of the record depends on logging before the outcome is known. On vetoes, I'd keep it minimal: reject any horizon other than H=12, reject private files lacking a public hash commitment, and reject premature promotion to LOG.md or the dashboard.

I'd also need to correct a couple of attribution errors in the secretary's matrix — the claim about Fable's and Argon's resolved zeros isn't right, and the mean-8 convention claim attributed to me was actually a mistake on my part. I'm aiming to keep the whole response tight, around 600 words.
